title: Quotation accuracy in medical journal articles — a systematic review and meta-analysis

extracted.subtask_description: Pools decades of studies auditing whether citations in published medical articles actually support the claims attached to them, establishing a stable cross-study taxonomy of citation/quotation error and verification methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation accuracy vs quotation accuracy distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation accuracy = correctness of the bibliographic information (author names, journal, volume, page numbers, year) - i.e., does the reference list entry correctly describe the source, independent of what it's used to claim. Quotation accuracy = 'the correctness of the content of a literature reference, that is, whether the reference supports or is in accordance with the statement by citing authors' - a semantic/content check, not a formatting check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A citation can be bibliographically perfect (correct authors/pages/DOI) while still being a total quotation error (the source says something different from, or unrelated to, the claim), and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major error - not at all in accordance with the claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Major error defined as 'seriously misrepresenting or bearing no resemblance to the original source' (De Lacey et al.'s canonical formulation, one of the earliest and most frequently reused definitions), operationalized by Luo et al. (2013) as references that 'contradicted, failed to substantiate, or were irrelevant to the author's assertion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This decomposition (contradiction / failure-to-substantiate / irrelevance) is itself a useful 3-way split within 'major error' and maps closely onto NLI-style SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NEUTRAL-type labels used in later NLP work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor error - misleading but not meaning-altering
rubrics_metrics.description: Inconsistencies and factual errors not severe enough to contradict a statement by citing authors. De Lacey's original wording: the error 'misled or could mislead, but the errors were not sufficiently serious to destroy or fundamentally to alter the meaning.' The gist of the claim survives, but some detail (a number, a qualifier, a scope restriction) is wrong or fabricated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect/secondary reference flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations to a review article or secondary summary rather than to the original/primary source for a fact. Some studies fold this into 'minor error' (the claim may be technically supported by the chain of citations, but the immediate cited work is not where the evidence originates); others track it as a separate, non-error category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worth keeping as its own flag, since 'does the cited paper itself contain the evidence, or does it just cite someone else who does' is a distinct and checkable property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loose 'consistent with the gist' support standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Some studies counted a citation as 'correct' even when it was 'not logically accurate,' as long as the reference was serving as a supporting example consistent with the general point being made - i.e., a looser 'consistent with the gist' standard rather than strict entailment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-rate denominator convention (reference-based vs quotation-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors were counted three different ways across the literature: (1) reference-based, restricted - count at most one error per reference, regardless of how many quotation problems that single reference has; (2) reference-based, unrestricted - count every distinct error found against a given reference; (3) quotation-based - use each in-text citation instance (not each unique reference) as the denominator, so a reference cited five times contributes five denominators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This denominator choice alone can swing reported 'error rate' by a large factor between studies and is a critical methodological detail for anyone trying to compare or reproduce citation-accuracy numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability varies by error severity tier
rubrics_metrics.description: Pooled/average kappa across studies that reported it: κ ≈ 0.76 (substantial agreement). But reliability is not uniform across error severity: Reddy et al. (2008) found much lower agreement specifically for minor errors (κ = 0.26, near-chance-to-fair), attributed to 'subjective factors' in what counts as a 'misleading but not fundamentally altering' minor error versus a non-error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direct warning for claim-matching metrics: agreement on a coarse SUPPORT/NOT-SUPPORT binary will look much better than agreement on finer-grained partial-support judgments, and reported IAA numbers should be read at the granularity they were actually computed for.
